title: Always, Usually, Sometimes
description: Describe how often routine activities happen.
objectives: Describe how often routine activities happen.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to describe how often routine activities happen. The central language is frequency adverbs before main verbs and after be. It belongs to the practical context of daily life. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: frequency adverbs before main verbs and after be

blocks.english: I usually eat lunch at noon.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the always, usually, sometimes exchange.

blocks.english: We are sometimes busy on Friday.
blocks.explanation: This always, usually, sometimes model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: What do you do every day?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the always, usually, sometimes exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I usually eat lunch at noon.” and “We are sometimes busy on Friday.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: frequency adverbs before main verbs and after be.

Use one clear model, add a relevant detail, and respond to the other speaker.
